tasks.title: Add AbortController to RunningAgent and stop() to AgentRunnerService
tasks.description: Add an `AbortController` field to the `RunningAgent` interface. In `executePipeline()`, race `pipeline.run()` against the abort signal. Add `stop(issueId: string): Promise<boolean>` method to `AgentRunnerService` that aborts the controller, cleans up `activeAgents`, `pendingGates`, `waitingQuestions`, sets issue status to `blocked`, and emits `agent_stopped` event.
acceptanceCriteria: stop(issueId) returns true when agent is running and was stopped
stop(issueId) returns false when no agent is running for that issueId
stop() removes entry from activeAgents, pendingGates, and waitingQuestions
stop() sets issue status to blocked via issueRepo
stop() emits agent_stopped event with issueId, projectId, issueNumber
stop() handles race condition when agent finishes during stop (no throw)
tasks.notes: The AbortSignal must propagate through WorkflowController to createAcpConnection so the ACP prompt() call is interrupted. Add signal?: AbortSignal to WorkflowControllerOptions and AcpConnectionOptions.

tasks.title: Propagate AbortSignal through WorkflowController to ACP session
tasks.description: Add `signal?: AbortSignal` to `WorkflowControllerOptions` and `AcpConnectionOptions`. In `WorkflowController.run()`, check `signal.aborted` between stage transitions and reject if aborted. In `createAcpConnection()`, race the `prompt()` call against `signal` abort so the ACP session is interrupted immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: WorkflowController.run() checks signal.aborted between stages and throws AbortError
createAcpConnection prompt() races against signal abort
When signal fires, ACP connection.cancel() is called and subprocess killed
Pipeline promise resolves (via catch) when signal aborts mid-stage
tasks.notes: The AcpConnection already has connection.cancel() logic for timeouts (line 382, 766). Reuse the same pattern for abort signal.

tasks.title: Add POST /api/issues/:number/stop route
tasks.description: Add a new route handler for `POST /api/issues/:number/stop` in `createIssueRoutes()`. Validate project context (400), issue exists (404), agent is running (409), then call `agentRunner.stop(issue.id)` and return 200 with success message.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/issues/:number/stop returns 200 with { success: true, data: { message } } when agent stopped
Returns 409 when no agent running for the issue
tasks.notes: Follow the same pattern as the close handler — check project, check issue, check agent, then act.

tasks.title: Add force query parameter to close, reopen, approve, reject handlers
tasks.description: Modify the four handlers (close, reopen, approve, reject) to read `force` from query params. When `force=true` and agent is running, call `agentRunner.stop(issue.id)` first, then proceed with the original operation. Without `force`, keep existing 409 behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Without force param, all four endpoints still return 409 when agent running
Force param is no-op when no agent is running
tasks.notes: Extract a helper like `ensureAgentStopped(issueId, force)` to avoid duplicating the stop-then-check logic across four handlers.

tasks.title: Write tests for AgentRunnerService.stop() and AbortSignal propagation
tasks.description: Write unit tests for `stop()`: stop running agent, stop non-existent agent (returns false), race condition safety. Write tests for AbortSignal propagation through WorkflowController. Test the abort causes pipeline.run() to reject with AbortError.
acceptanceCriteria: stop() on running agent returns true and cleans up state
stop() on non-existent agent returns false
stop() during agent self-completion does not throw
tasks.notes: Mock WorkflowController to simulate long-running pipeline. Use real EventBus and in-memory DB.

tasks.title: Write API integration tests for stop endpoint and force parameter
tasks.description: Write integration tests using supertest for: POST /stop with running agent (200), POST /stop with no agent (409), POST /stop with missing issue (404), POST /close?force=true with running agent (200), POST /close without force with running agent (409), same for reopen/approve/reject.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /stop returns 200 when agent is running and stops it
POST /stop returns 409 when no agent running
POST /close?force=true returns 200 and closes after stopping agent
POST /close returns 409 without force when agent running
tasks.notes: Follow patterns from existing api-routes.test.ts. Mock AgentRunnerService.stop() to avoid needing real ACP subprocess.
